answer: Sybil resistance relies on bonded escrows: when k identities equivocate in a correlated way, pairwise evidence yields up to k(k−1)/2 accountable links, so penalties grow as O(k²), not linearly. Detection within the horizon triggers asymmetric depreciation, compounding the forfeiture across linked bonds; thus a coordinated swarm can suffer an exponential multiplier in capital loss. A monitor on a knoll may view the prism of shared behavior, but attribution still requires verifiable evidence.
